input: Research family ancestry using an online genealogy site

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Ancestry research can range from a single family line to a full multi-generational tree across multiple branches — knowing how deep or wide to go completely changes the workload.
Whether this is for the user personally, a specific relative (e.g. an aging parent), or a shared family project determines whose records to prioritise and who else is involved.
The geographic or ethnic origin of the family determines which records and genealogy databases are most relevant and accessible.
Most major genealogy sites (Ancestry, MyHeritage, Findmypast) require paid subscriptions — knowing the budget determines which platform and features are usable.
The user may already have an account on a specific platform, or have existing records/documents on hand — this affects the starting point and avoids redundant setup steps.
The end goal could be anything from a basic family tree chart to DNA ethnicity results, historical document collection, or a written family narrative — this defines what 'done' looks like.
Some people want to do the research themselves for the experience; others want the fastest path to results — this shapes how the plan is structured and how much guidance to provide.

gold.taskTitle: Research family ancestry using an online genealogy site
gold.taskDescription: The user wants to explore their family history and build out an ancestry record using an online genealogy platform.

questions.title: How many generations back do you want to trace?
questions.description: Determines the depth and scope of the research — e.g. grandparents only, or as far back as records allow.

questions.title: Who is this research primarily for?
questions.description: Identifies whether this is a personal project, a gift for a family member, or a collaborative family effort — shaping whose records are the focus.

questions.title: Which country or region does your family originate from?
questions.description: The geographic and ethnic origin of the family determines which databases, record archives, and genealogy platforms will be most relevant.

questions.title: Are you open to paying for a genealogy site subscription?
questions.description: Budget constraints determine which platforms and premium features (e.g. historical records, DNA matching) are viable options.

questions.title: Do you already have an account or existing family tree started?
questions.description: Knowing the starting point — existing accounts, prior research, or physical documents on hand — avoids redundant setup steps.

questions.title: What does a successful outcome look like to you?
questions.description: The end goal could be a visual family tree, a collection of historical documents, DNA ethnicity results, or a written narrative — this defines what 'done well' means.

questions.title: Do you prefer to research yourself or get results quickly?
questions.description: Some users want a hands-on discovery experience; others want the fastest path to answers — this shapes how prescriptive and step-by-step the plan should be.
